tasks.title: take: a done record must not close a brief as queued
tasks.why: P1, still standing from 2026-10-17 at its new line. briefs.py:544-560: when queued_on finds the unit only in the board's relay/done, stands is 'done', the refusal at 553 fires only on `not stands`, and answer() is called with queued=<uid> and done_already='an earlier unit of that id'. The brief closes saying it was queued although nothing stands on the relay's queue and no session will ever run it; became_of (briefs.py:479) only adds that the relay has a done record of that id, and the brief is gone from waiting(). That is the exact failure the guard above it was written to stop ('a yes of his taken up without the work being queued is his word dropped'). The board has 1122 relay/done records today, and unit ids are slugged from titles, so a new yes meeting an old record of the same name is not a corner case. No commit in 6959ad81..origin/integration touches it.
tasks.done_when: a test in Tools/assetboard/test_briefstates.py puts the unit only in the board's relay/done, commits and pushes it to the board's origin/main, and asserts take either refuses (naming that only a done record exists) or closes the brief with no 'queued' key and an outcome that says nothing was queued; red on today's code

tasks.title: queued_on: read the board in one pass, tolerate a bad file
tasks.why: P2. briefs.py:287-307: queued_on lists relay/queue and relay/done and then spawns `git show` once per json file (line 294). The board carries 1122 of them today and git sorts all of relay/done before any relay/queue, so a unit that does stand on the queue is found only after about 1100 subprocesses: every brief close waits a minute or more on Windows, and take() calls this on the owner's live yes. Worse, line 299-300 turns any single unparseable file under relay/queue or relay/done into a failed read of the whole board, so take() then refuses with 'the board could not be read' and the brief stays open even though the unit plainly stands on the queue - one junk or half-written record on the board blocks every answer until somebody finds it. The old code skipped such a file (`continue`); the 2026-10-16 fix for telling why a read failed widened it to an abort.
tasks.done_when: a test in Tools/assetboard/test_briefstates.py commits a unit in relay/queue plus a file of junk bytes in relay/done, and asserts queued_on returns ('queue', '') - not a failed read - and that it reads the tree in one git call (count the git invocations, or assert it stays under a handful with 50 done records); red on today's code
